title: each registered external project can name its own worker and reviewer vendor and fallback list in its private state/config.yaml, read by the one vendor resolver every launcher uses, so fm-dispatch, the autopilot and hand launches start that project's rounds on the configured vendor and the identity records rule=project
acceptance: Why. The captain (2026-10-07): each repository must be configurable to run its worker rounds on a different agent, and this goes before T-237. Today the worker vendor is engine-level: bin/fm-config.sh fm_vendor_rule (:480-485) reads `<role>: vendor:` and then the top-level `vendor:` only from FM_CONFIG, which fm_storage_init (:945) always sets to the engine config.yaml, also for an external project. fm-worker.sh accepts --vendor, but fm-dispatch and the autopilot never pass it, so an external project's rounds always resolve `opposite-of-host` (a Claude host gives a codex worker).

Change 1, the role vendor (bin/fm-config.sh fm_vendor_rule, :480-485). When FM_EXTERNAL=1 and "$FM_STATE_DIR/config.yaml" exists, read `<role>: vendor:` from that private file first; a value there wins over every engine value. Otherwise behave exactly as today, whatever file argument the caller passes. A new helper fm_vendor_source <role> prints `project` when the private value was used, else `engine`. fm_role_vendor and fm_vendor_chain keep their signatures and pick this up through fm_vendor_rule. The self project keeps its existing override, the `worker:`/`reviewer:` blocks in the engine config.yaml (:21-23); no new self key.

Change 2, the fallback list (bin/fm-config.sh). The private list uses the `- item` line form that fm_cfg_list (:43-48) and the board (server.ts:446) read, for example `fallback:
  - codex`. When FM_EXTERNAL=1 and the private file's `fallback:` list has at least one `- item` entry, that list replaces the engine list in two places: the trailing `fm_cfg_list fallback` in fm_vendor_chain (:500), and the unknown-or-unconfirmed-host head in fm_role_vendor (:518). An empty or missing private list uses the engine list. A private `fallback:` line carrying an inline value (the bracket form `fallback: [codex]` that onboarding writes for other keys, fm_onboard.py:298-300) is not read as a list: fm_vendor_chain prints `fm-vendor: <private file>: fallback must use '- vendor' lines; using the engine fallback list` on stderr and uses the engine list. The `opposite-of-host` pair step (:493-499) is unchanged and still comes before the fallback list. Example: private `worker:
  vendor: claude` and `fallback:
  - codex` give the worker chain exactly `claude`, `codex`.

Change 3, the model stays per vendor (T-146). fm_model_for (:564-576) uses the engine `<role>: model:` only when the vendor equals the role vendor that the engine file alone resolves (the same resolver evaluated with FM_EXTERNAL=0), and the top-level `model:` under the same engine-only comparison. Without this, Change 1 would hand an engine `worker: {vendor: codex, model: <codex model>}` override to a project's claude worker. No private `<role>: model:` is added; a project's vendor uses the engine `models.<vendor>`.

Change 4, the record. fm_record_vendor_resolution writes rule=`project` when fm_vendor_source returns project and the value is a named vendor; a private `opposite-of-host` value records rule `opposite-of-host` as today. An explicit --vendor still records rule `explicit` and still wins, because fm_vendor_chain returns the explicit vendor alone (:488). fm_log_vendor_resolution keeps its line format, so the worker log reads `fm-vendor: host=claude rule=project resolved=claude`. bin/lib/fm_config_runtime.py:32-37 stores any rule string and needs no change.

Change 5, engine-wide session report. bin/fm-session.sh:27 runs fm_storage_init with no project argument, so an external default_project makes FM_EXTERNAL=1 there. Its start-only report (:61-83) describes the engine config.yaml: run `fm_model reviewer config.yaml` at :62 and the fm_role_vendor/fm_model_for pair at :78 with FM_EXTERNAL=0 for those calls only. Without this, Changes 1 and 3 would make :62 resolve the private reviewer vendor and report the engine reviewer model as missing.

Not changed, stated. fm_run_chain's adapter check stays as it is: a head with no adapter returns 65 (:747-750) and later unknown vendors are skipped (:752), for private and engine lists alike. The refusal text at bin/fm-worker.sh:1566-1567 and bin/fm-review.sh:1092-1093 keeps naming $FM_CONFIG even when the private file named the head; that wording is accepted and out of scope. bin/fm-canary.sh:188 never calls fm_storage_init and stays engine-only with no change.

Binding and pins (no code change). Before dispatch (no pin) fm_binding.py:73-74 hashes the live private state/config.yaml into contract_sha256, so adding a vendor or fallback key changes that digest and readiness (:350-352, :374-375) asks for a fresh judgement, as any edit to that file does today. After dispatch fm_binding.py:66-71 hashes the pinned `contract` snapshot, and fm_spec_pins.py:448-449 and :484-485 keep that pin without a repin decision: the edit changes no digest, the task does not re-gate, and the new vendor applies from the task's next launch, because the launchers resolve the vendor from the live file. Gates read only the `project:` block (fm_spec_pins.contract :44-59 -> fm-herdr project_contract), so the new top-level keys never change gate commands.

Tests, new behaviour (each fails on the base commit, passes after). tests/project-vendor.test.sh driving tests/lib/project_vendor.py, in the style of tests/lib/firstmate_host.py (scrubbed env, copied bin/, stub CLIs, temp engine with `vendor: opposite-of-host` and a claude host record, temp FM_STATE_DIR, FM_EXTERNAL=1): (1) private `worker: vendor: claude` gives fm_role_vendor worker = claude [Change 1]; (2) private `reviewer:
  vendor: claude` gives fm_role_vendor reviewer = claude [Change 1; on base the engine opposite-of-host rule with the claude host gives codex]; (3) private `worker:
  vendor: claude` with `fallback:
  - codex` (line form) gives fm_vendor_chain worker exactly `claude
codex` [Change 2]; (4) with no host record and a private `fallback:\n  - codex` under a private `worker: vendor: opposite-of-host`, fm_role_vendor worker = codex, not the engine head [Change 2]; (5) engine `worker:
  vendor: codex
  model: gpt-x` with private `worker: vendor: claude` gives `fm_model worker` = the engine models.claude, not gpt-x [Change 3; on base fm_model worker returns gpt-x]; (6a) a private `fallback: [codex]` bracket line prints the `must use '- vendor' lines` warning and the chain ends with the engine list [Change 2]; (6) fm_record_vendor_resolution worker "" writes {host: claude, rule: project, vendor: claude} [Change 4].

Tests, regression (pass on base and after). In the same suite: FM_EXTERNAL=0 ignores the private file; an explicit vendor gives a one-line chain and records rule explicit; an empty private fallback list keeps the engine list; `fm_model_for worker claude` with the Change 3 config returns models.claude; with no pin the binding digest of the private file changes after adding a vendor key, and with a pin it does not; fm_spec_pins.contract() returns the same project contract with and without the new top-level keys. tests/session-startup.test.sh, a new start case [Change 5]. fm-session.sh uses one file for two things: the registry reader loads bin/fm-herdr.py as a module (bin/fm-config.sh:338 -> bin/lib/fm_registry.py:18-19, :57, :70), and the session engine runs it as a script, `exec python3 "${FM_CODE_ROOT:-$REPO}/bin/fm-herdr.py" session ...` (bin/fm-session.sh:106). The existing reviewer_report harness overwrites that file with a one-line stub (tests/session-startup.test.sh:136), which breaks the registry, so this case does not use it. Instead it copies the real file to bin/fm-herdr-real.py in the test repo and writes bin/fm-herdr.py as a shim: at import it loads fm-herdr-real.py with importlib and copies its public names into its own module namespace, so the registry reader gets the real project_contract, project_field and _project_scalar; run as a script with first argument `session`, it prints `FM_EXTERNAL=` and `FM_STATE_DIR=` from its environment and exits 0; run as a script with any other argument it runs fm-herdr-real.py through runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__'). Only the `session` script call is stubbed; the registry parsing is real. config.yaml registers an external default_project (FM_HOME passed to a temp dir), names `reviewer:
  vendor: claude
  model: claude-opus-5-5` and no models.codex, and the private file names `reviewer:
  vendor: codex` and `worker:
  vendor: claude`. Run `fm-session.sh start` the way reviewer_report does (FM_ENTRY_PID/FM_ENTRY_SCRIPT, scrubbed FM_* env plus FM_HOME). Assert stdout has FM_EXTERNAL=1 and the private state dir (the project really resolved as external), and stderr has no `names no reviewer`. With Changes 1 and 3 but not Change 5 this case fails, because :62 resolves codex and finds no model; on base it passes, so it is a regression guard. tests/lib/firstmate_host.py, tests/config.test.sh (:391-414, :598-606, :610-645), tests/canary.test.sh:149 and tests/adapter-verdict.test.sh:73-132 run without FM_EXTERNAL and stay green unchanged.

Callers, all listed. bin/fm-worker.sh:95-97, :1496, :1532; bin/fm-review.sh:113-115, :363, :1006; bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh:44-46, :52, :86; bin/fm-session.sh:62, :78 (Change 5); bin/fm-canary.sh:188 (unchanged); fm_run_chain :771 inside bin/fm-config.sh. fm-dispatch and the autopilot start rounds through bin/fm-worker.sh after fm_storage_init sets FM_EXTERNAL and FM_STATE_DIR (:978-980), so they pick up the project vendor with no change. bin/fm-doctor.sh:57-59 and bin/fm-setup.sh:191-193 are engine-only and unchanged.

Migration. No stored record format changes. Existing private config files have no `worker:`, `reviewer:` or `fallback:` keys, so every existing project resolves, records and binds exactly as before. Adding a key changes the contract digest only for a task not yet dispatched (see Binding and pins). Existing identity.json records keep their rule values.

Docs. design/design.md §5.3 (the vendor paragraph at :615-636, including :623-624 on the other main vendor before the fallbacks) and §15.3 (:5055): edit in place to say an external project may name `worker:`/`reviewer:` vendor and a non-empty `fallback:` list in `- item` form in its private state/config.yaml, that the bracket form is reported and ignored, that the private list replaces only the engine fallback list and keeps the opposite-of-host pair step before it, the rule=project record, that a dispatched task picks up a change at its next launch without a re-gate, and that re-running onboarding rewrites the private file from the contract (fm_onboard.py:300) and drops these hand-added keys, so they are added again after it. Same in bin/adapters/_contract.md:155-162 and skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:1205-1212. No new numbered section.

Not in this task, a follow-up. The board badge (board/server.ts engine(), :433-457) keeps reading only the engine config.yaml and keeps showing the engine rule; it does not show a project's private vendor. Its existing tests (tests/board-readiness.test.sh:46-62, tests/e2e/firstmate-host.spec.ts:53, tests/e2e/board-engine-rule.spec.ts:6-21) are untouched. A later task makes the badge read the selected project's private file.

intent.text: Each external project can name the vendor that runs its worker rounds.
Each external project can name its own fallback list.
Dispatch, the autopilot and hand launches all start the round on that vendor.
The round identity records that the project chose the vendor.

why.text: On 2026-10-07 you asked that each repository can use a different worker agent, before T-237.
Today one engine rule picks the worker vendor for every project.
For one external project you chose codex as the only fallback.

scope_in: a new project vendor suite and a session case
design, adapter contract and skill text
scope_out: the adapter check and its refusal text

done.text: Intent 1: the resolver reads the role vendor from the private project config first. The new suite proves it.
Intent 2: a non-empty private fallback list replaces the engine list. The new suite proves it.
Intent 3: every launcher selects the project first and then calls the same resolver. The caller list and the suite prove it.
Intent 4: the identity records rule project. The new suite proves it.

notes.text: With no private fallback key, the engine fallback list still applies.
A dispatched task keeps its pinned contract and uses a new vendor from its next launch.
The board badge still shows the engine rule. A later task changes it.

intent.text: 每個外部專案都能指定執行 worker 回合的廠商。
每個外部專案都能指定自己的備援清單。
派工、autopilot 和手動啟動都用那個廠商開始回合。
回合身分記錄廠商由專案指定。

why.text: 你在 2026-10-07 要求每個 repo 能用不同的 worker，並排在 T-237 之前。
現在一條引擎規則替所有專案選 worker 廠商。
你替一個外部專案選了 codex 當唯一的備援。

scope_in: bin/fm-config.sh 的廠商和模型解析
新的專案廠商測試和啟動案例
design、adapter 契約和 skill 文字

done.text: 意圖 1：解析器先讀私有專案設定的角色廠商。新測試證明。

意圖 3：選定專案後，每個啟動方式都走同一個解析器。呼叫清單和測試證明。

notes.text: 私有設定沒有備援鍵時，仍套用引擎的備援清單。
已派工的任務保留固定的契約，下一次啟動才用新廠商。
看板標籤仍顯示引擎規則，由後續任務修改。
